title: High Pressure Protection
shortDescription: High refrigerant pressure detected — system shut down.
fullDescription: E1 on a Lennox AC indicates the high pressure switch tripped due to excessive condenser pressure.
safetyWarning: Do not open refrigerant connections. Turn off system before inspecting.

fixSteps.title: Clean Condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Hose down outdoor coils from inside out.

fixSteps.title: Clear Unit Area
fixSteps.instruction: Maintain 2+ feet clearance around outdoor unit.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning does not resolve the issue.

faq.a: Yes, only a professional should adjust charge.

title: Anti-Freeze Protection — Evaporator
shortDescription: The indoor coil is at risk of freezing.
fullDescription: E2 indicates the evaporator coil temperature dropped near freezing. The compressor shuts down to prevent ice damage.
safetyWarning: Let all ice melt before restarting. Running a frozen system damages the compressor.

fixSteps.title: Thaw
fixSteps.instruction: Run fan-only mode for 2-4 hours to melt ice.

fixSteps.title: Open Vents
fixSteps.instruction: All supply and return vents open.

whenToCallPro: If problem recurs after new filter — likely low refrigerant.

faq.a: Usually dirty filter or low refrigerant.
No, you may damage the coil. Let it melt naturally.
It can destroy the compressor if run frozen.

title: Low Pressure Protection
fullDescription: E3 indicates the low pressure switch tripped, typically from a refrigerant leak or metering restriction.
safetyWarning: Only EPA-certified technicians can handle refrigerant. Turn off system to prevent compressor damage.

fixSteps.title: Check for Leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Look for oil stains at connections.

fixSteps.title: Check Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Replace filter to rule out airflow issues.

fixSteps.title: Turn Off
fixSteps.instruction: Stop the system to protect the compressor.

faq.a: No, it is illegal without EPA certification.
No, the leak must be found and repaired.

title: Compressor Discharge Temperature High
fullDescription: E4 indicates the compressor discharge temperature exceeded safe limits, risking compressor damage.
safetyWarning: Turn off the AC to prevent permanent compressor damage.
whenToCallPro: If cleaning does not resolve it.

faq.a: Yes, it can cause permanent winding damage.
Turn off the AC and get it checked soon.

title: Compressor Overcurrent
fullDescription: E5 indicates the compressor exceeded its rated amperage, triggering overcurrent protection.
safetyWarning: High current can cause fire. Turn off at disconnect. Do not keep restarting.

fixSteps.title: Clean Condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Reduce compressor load by cleaning coils.

faq.q: Does this mean a new AC?
faq.a: Not necessarily — could be a capacitor.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Communication failure between indoor and outdoor units.
fullDescription: E6 indicates the indoor and outdoor units cannot communicate, typically due to wiring issues or a control board failure.
safetyWarning: Turn off both units before inspecting wiring.
symptoms: One unit runs, other does not

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off both units for 5 minutes, restart.

whenToCallPro: If power cycling and wire checks fail.

faq.a: The low-voltage signal wire between units.

title: Outdoor Ambient Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The outdoor ambient temperature sensor has failed.
fullDescription: Code 271 indicates the outdoor ambient temperature sensor (thermistor) has failed or is reading out of range.
safetyWarning: Turn off the outdoor unit before inspecting.
symptoms: Abnormal operation in heat pump mode

fixSteps.title: Check Connection
fixSteps.instruction: Verify sensor wire is plugged in.

whenToCallPro: If replacement does not fix it.

faq.a: Measures outdoor temp for system optimization.
Some systems will run in limited mode.

title: Outdoor Coil Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The outdoor coil temperature sensor has failed.
fullDescription: Code 292 indicates the outdoor coil thermistor is defective or disconnected.
safetyWarning: Turn off the outdoor unit disconnect before working on the unit.
whenToCallPro: If replacement does not resolve the issue.

faq.a: Monitors outdoor coil temp for defrost timing.
Defrost will not work properly in heat pump mode.

title: Voltage Protection — High or Low
shortDescription: Supply voltage is outside acceptable range.
fullDescription: P1 indicates the supply voltage to the Lennox outdoor unit is too high or too low for safe operation.
safetyWarning: Do not modify electrical connections. Voltage problems may be a utility or wiring issue.

fixSteps.title: Wait
fixSteps.instruction: Wait 30 minutes for utility voltage to stabilize.

fixSteps.title: Monitor Voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Check voltage at disconnect with multimeter.

fixSteps.title: Call Electrician
fixSteps.instruction: Persistent voltage issues need electrical panel inspection.

faq.a: A single occurrence during a storm is usually fine.
Yes, for areas with frequent fluctuations.

title: Indoor Fan Motor Error
shortDescription: The indoor blower motor has malfunctioned.
fullDescription: H6 indicates the indoor fan motor is stalled, overcurrent, or not responding to the control board.
safetyWarning: Turn off system. A stalled motor can overheat.

fixSteps.title: Check for Blockage
fixSteps.instruction: Open unit and check for debris blocking the fan.

fixSteps.title: Spin Fan
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, spin fan by hand. Resistance = bad bearings.

whenToCallPro: If fan does not spin freely.

faq.q: Can I run without the fan?

title: Outdoor Coil Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor coil temperature sensor open or short circuit.
fullDescription: E121 indicates the outdoor coil thermistor is faulty or disconnected. System may run inefficiently or shut down.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Locate outdoor coil sensor; check for damage.

title: Low Pressure Trip
fullDescription: E223 on Lennox iComfort indicates the low-side pressure switch opened. Likely refrigerant leak or restricted airflow.

title: High Pressure Trip
shortDescription: High pressure switch opened — discharge pressure exceeded limit.
fullDescription: E230 means HPS opened on Lennox AC. Most often dirty outdoor coil or fan problem.

title: Compressor Top Cap Switch Open
shortDescription: Compressor internal overload tripped from overheating.
fullDescription: E240 indicates the compressor internal thermal switch (Klixon) opened from heat or current overload.

title: Discharge Line Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E270 means the discharge line thermistor is open, shorted, or out of range. Affects compressor protection logic.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Compare resistance to spec at ambient.

title: Outdoor Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor fan motor reported failure or no feedback.
fullDescription: E292 indicates the variable-speed outdoor fan motor is faulty or its tach signal missing.

title: Low 24V Voltage
shortDescription: 24VAC supply to control is below operating range.
fullDescription: E200 means the secondary transformer voltage is low. Caused by overload, shorted accessory, or weak transformer.

title: Loss of Communication With Thermostat
shortDescription: Indoor unit lost comm with iComfort thermostat for 3+ minutes.
fullDescription: E124 indicates RSBus communication failure between indoor blower and thermostat.

faq.a: Yes — i+ and i- must not be swapped.

title: Indoor Coil Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E180 indicates an open or shorted indoor coil sensor used for freeze and dehumidification logic.

faq.a: Yes if you can access coil cabinet.

title: Low Line Voltage
shortDescription: Incoming 240V line voltage low for outdoor unit.
fullDescription: E115 means the outdoor unit detected line voltage below safe operating range.

faq.a: Only if sized for AC startup.

title: iComfort Communications Bus Loss
shortDescription: Indoor unit lost RSBus communication with thermostat.
fullDescription: Error E105 means the iComfort RSBus link between the indoor unit, thermostat, and outdoor unit dropped. Communicating Lennox systems require all four wires functional.

fixSteps.title: Tighten Terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat all 4 wires at thermostat and indoor unit.

fixSteps.title: Replace Cable
fixSteps.instruction: Pull new 18/4 thermostat cable if damaged.

whenToCallPro: Cable runs through walls usually need a pro.

faq.a: Yes — communicating units cannot run without bus.
Some Lennox models allow legacy 24V mode via dip switch.

title: Outdoor Unit Communication Loss
shortDescription: Indoor cannot reach outdoor over RSBus.
fullDescription: E106 specifies the indoor board reached the thermostat but lost the outdoor unit on the RSBus. Wire between indoor and outdoor is the prime suspect.

fixSteps.title: Check 24V at Outdoor Board
fixSteps.instruction: Measure between R and C — should be 24VAC.

fixSteps.title: Replace Board
fixSteps.instruction: If 24V present but no comms, outdoor control needs replacement.

whenToCallPro: When the outdoor board itself is dead.

faq.a: Yes — surge events frequently kill outdoor comm boards.

title: Outdoor Discharge Line Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Discharge line thermistor open or short.
fullDescription: E311 indicates the outdoor unit's discharge line thermistor is reading invalid values. Lennox uses this sensor for compressor protection.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Find sensor on discharge line at compressor; check clip.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Clip new sensor to discharge line.

whenToCallPro: If sensor is good and wired correctly, the outdoor board has failed.

faq.a: To predict refrigerant problems before compressor damage.
Lennox-spec sensor recommended; exact resistance curve matters.

title: Outdoor Suction Line Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E312 indicates the suction-line thermistor is open or shorted, preventing the outdoor controller from calculating superheat.
symptoms: Variable-capacity unit may run at fixed speed
whenToCallPro: If swapping the sensor doesn't clear it, suspect the outdoor board.

faq.a: No — different placement and sometimes different curve.

title: Compressor Top Cap Switch Open
fullDescription: E347 means the compressor's top-cap thermal switch opened. The compressor itself is overheating and the safety cut its 24V circuit.

fixSteps.title: Replace Switch
fixSteps.instruction: If switch failed open cold, swap top-cap switch.

whenToCallPro: Repeated trips usually mean charge or compressor wear — pro required.

faq.a: Yes after cooldown, but it'll trip again if root cause not fixed.

title: Outdoor Fan Lockout
shortDescription: Outdoor fan motor RPM mismatch lockout.
fullDescription: E380 fires after repeated outdoor fan faults. The control measures back-EMF and locks the unit out to prevent compressor damage from no airflow.

fixSteps.title: Visual Check
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; spin fan by hand to feel for binding.

fixSteps.title: Test Capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: Check microfarad rating with capacitance meter.

fixSteps.title: Replace Cap or Motor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap capacitor first; if motor windings open, replace motor.

whenToCallPro: ECM-style fans require model-specific replacement modules.

faq.a: Yes — discharge it with an insulated screwdriver before handling.

safetyWarning: Capacitors store lethal charge. Always discharge before touching terminals.

title: Compressor Locked Rotor
shortDescription: Compressor draws stall current, can't start.
fullDescription: E400 indicates the inverter/start kit detected locked-rotor amperage on the compressor — the compressor cannot turn.

fixSteps.title: Check Start Components
fixSteps.instruction: Test start cap and PTCR/start kit.

fixSteps.title: Add Hard-Start
fixSteps.instruction: Hard-start kit can rescue weak compressors.

whenToCallPro: Compressor swaps are a serious job — get multiple quotes.

faq.a: If compressor under warranty + unit <8 yrs, fix; else replace.

title: Compressor Lockout (Multiple Trips)
shortDescription: Compressor protection lockout after repeated faults.
fullDescription: E405 is a safety lockout — Lennox saw too many compressor faults in a 24-hour window and disabled it until manually reset.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Cut power 5 minutes to reset lockout for diagnosis.

fixSteps.title: Address Root Cause
fixSteps.instruction: Don't just reset — find and fix the underlying fault.

whenToCallPro: E405 always — repeated lockouts indicate something serious.

faq.q: Can I just keep resetting it?
faq.a: No — you'll cook the compressor and void warranty.

title: Indoor Airflow Insufficient
fullDescription: Lennox iComfort variable-capacity blowers measure static pressure. E411 means the system cannot achieve required CFM at any tap.

fixSteps.title: Open Registers
fixSteps.instruction: Walk the home; open all supply vents.

fixSteps.title: Check Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM-spec MERV — replace high-MERV with standard.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Ductwork
fixSteps.instruction: Look in attic/crawl for crushed or disconnected flex.

whenToCallPro: If duct system is undersized, professional duct redesign needed.

faq.a: Yes — closing more than 20% of registers spikes static pressure.

title: Outdoor Inverter Over-Temperature
fullDescription: E590 means the inverter heat sink reached its thermal limit. Inverter throttles or shuts off to protect IGBTs.

fixSteps.title: Clean Heat Sink
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum dust from inverter housing vents.

fixSteps.title: Provide Shade
fixSteps.instruction: Long-term: shade outdoor unit (without restricting airflow).

faq.q: Why now and not last year?
faq.a: Dust accumulates over time and ambient temps may have set new records.
